title: Conservative Auto‑Tuner for Batching & KV Cache in Private (audit‑first rollout)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a conservative, audit‑first auto‑tuner for batching and KV cache recommendations targeted at Private/VPC/on‑prem deployments. The feature must operate in a dry‑run (offline) mode by default, produce human‑readable recommendations, and support a guarded apply path with automatic rollback hooks compatible with restricted networking and KMS/HSM constraints.
acceptance_criteria: Dry‑run mode runs in Private clusters without outbound network egress and produces a JSON + human summary of suggested batching and KV cache changes
Recommendations include expected cost delta, latency impact distribution, and risk flags (e.g., cache eviction, tokenization mismatch)
Guarded apply requires explicit auditor approval or an automated policy check; unsafe actions blocked by policy engine before apply
Rollback plan is generated with a one‑click revert that works in offline/on‑prem environments and logs audit entries to customer‑managed storage
Integration tests simulate VPC restrictions and HSM/KMS unavailability and validate no secret exfiltration paths
Console surfaces a read‑only preview, diff of config changes, and per‑route token cost estimate for Private deployments

decisions: Default mode is dry‑run/offline to avoid unintended changes in restricted environments
Recommendations are conservative by default (only suggest changes with >= 10% cost saving and <5% expected p99 regression), configurable by admin
Apply path must be explicit and combinable with customer policy; we will not perform blind auto‑apply in Private
We will avoid reliance on external ML endpoints; recommendation heuristics run locally on control plane in VPC or on‑prem service
KV cache tweaks are limited to bucketed suggestions (e.g., increase cache size for high hit routes) rather than automatic eviction policy changes
notes: Tradeoffs: More aggressive autotune would yield higher cost savings but increases risk of latency regressions; customers running SLO‑sensitive services prefer conservative suggestions
On‑prem constraints: No external telemetry collection; must rely on sampled traces and local metrics. Encrypted metrics upload requires customer opt‑in.
KMS/HSM: When KMS unavailable, apply flow must fall back to manual signed approval stored to customer audit path
Compatibility: Must work with Dedicated and Private; ensure model variant fallbacks are surfaced as part of recommendations
Security: Work with Security early to ensure offline analyzer cannot be used to enumerate model fingerprints or prompt contents
